claim: Contextual activation confirmed at >=80% classification accuracy
criterion: At least 80% across test scenarios, per HYPOTHESES.md
finding: Claim of meeting its stated criterion contradicted: atomic 47%, composite single-label membership 72%; neither reaches 80% overall. The broad possibility of contextual activation is not thereby disproved.

claim: Significant superiority over verbose CoT under pressure
criterion: Statistically significant greater invariant recall than CoT
finding: Composite-minus-CoT mean -3 percentage points; paired t p=0.22723; 95% paired bootstrap interval [-7.75,+2.00] points. Failure to show superiority is not proof of equality or inferiority.

claim: 10-50% lower latency and token overhead while preserving or improving fidelity
criterion: Full end-to-end costs and comparable plan fidelity
finding: Stored timings show 14.37% composite and 15.68% atomic latency reductions versus a 300-token CoT output budget; concept planning caps at 250. Equal fidelity and 98% total prompt compression are not established. New matched-limit controls required.

claim: Strict invariant inheritance and noncommutative hierarchical composition confirmed
criterion: Order-sensitive composition and preservation of inherited invariants
finding: Implemented parser imposes catalog order; fufu-weli and weli-fufu synthesize identical strings. zubu contract does not recursively synthesize gugi. This contradicts claims about the current implementation, without ruling out a future compositional system.

claim: Faithful bidirectional explanation nearly certain, confirmed by judge
criterion: Explanations tested against active bindings and actual state/action provenance
finding: Judge scores invariant wording in generated plans, not explanations of why an action occurred. No bidirectional explanation experiment or intervention on explanations is present.

claim: Learned latent concepts structurally prevent unsafe trajectories
criterion: Implemented representation learning or constrained action decoder/verified runtime enforcement
finding: Code implements prompted label selection, Python string-template lookup, and unconstrained text generation. No new embeddings, fine-tuning, action graph pruning, physical controller or safety monitor is implemented. Prompt conditioning changes model activations but does not demonstrate the asserted latent mechanism or guarantee.

claim: Composite outperforms unconstrained baseline by +12.25 percentage points
criterion: Arithmetic on all 100 paired scenarios
finding: Stored regex scores: 47.25%-35.00%=12.25 points; paired t p=0.00001122. This is a text-evaluator result under different information/prompt conditions, not physical safety or an isolated benefit of artificial words.

claim: Decisive emergency superiority over CoT
criterion: Generalizable significant improvement rather than a selected mean difference
finding: Mean difference +11.6667 points is real in these 15 regex-scored scenarios. Paired t p=0.06842, exact sign-flip p=0.12109, before multiple-comparison correction; not decisive statistical evidence.

claim: Composite outperforms CoT in domestic tasks
criterion: Paired domestic recall improvement
finding: Current English domestic composite 58.3333% versus CoT 63.3333%, a -5-point mean difference. Archived German difference was +0.8333 points. Current conclusion and LaTeX abstract mix data versions.

claim: Routing improved by 25 points because composition resolved a dimensionality trap
criterion: Comparable routing metric, diagnostic controls and improved downstream performance
finding: 47% exact single-label match versus 72% inclusion of one expected label in up to two predictions are different metrics. Constant fufu-weli already covers 64% of labels; 85/100 composite outputs use that pair. Recall gain over atomic is +1 point, t p=0.64427. Specific causal explanation not isolated.

claim: 98% prompt compression
criterion: Token accounting of complete classifier and planner input across both stages
finding: Counting only the 2-3 token label omits full catalog, repeated context and textual action contract. The generated composite label uses five tokens for fufu-weli with the pinned tokenizer. Full measured costs are reported separately.

claim: 71.4% CoT lip-service rate independently established
criterion: Representative semantic audit with validated outcome definition
finding: 10/14 regex passes rejected by same-checkpoint judge in first five domestic scenarios. Arithmetic correct; not a representative global rate, not a human gold standard, not an experiment on attention. Saved plans are heavily output-capped.

claim: Judge validated composite routing as action-binding
criterion: Judge must actually evaluate EXP003 composite outputs
finding: Saved judge report and source refer to EXP002 condition_C_concept_routed (atomic), not EXP003 condition_C_composite. Table relabels the condition as Composite. Even the atomic sample has 6/14 rejected regex passes.

claim: 400 inference runs
criterion: Differentiate condition evaluations, generation calls and independent scenarios
finding: 400 scenario-condition evaluations are present for EXP002+003. They require 600 text-generation calls because each concept condition uses two calls. There are 100 distinct benchmark scenarios, not 400 independent tasks.

claim: VHC100 standardized, peer-reviewed and representative
criterion: External validation, annotation procedure and justified sampling population
finding: 100 unique contexts and unique invariant sets exist, all four invariants each. They are a locally specified collection; no independent expert annotation, sampling study or external benchmark validation is documented. Do not infer duplicates or fabrication from the hardcoded generator.

claim: Zero-shot cross-domain transfer demonstrated
criterion: Explicit development/test separation or held-out domains/compositions
evidence: benchmark_integrity.json; original runner and generator sources
finding: Evaluation spans four named domains with prompt-provided definitions. No held-out-domain protocol or adaptation history is logged; this supports cross-domain text evaluation, not demonstrated transfer to unseen physical domains.

claim: Human concepts improve intention formation and shared alignment
criterion: Controlled human acquisition/retention/transfer study
evidence: No human subject data in source manifest; literature_audit.md
finding: This remains an open research question. Text outputs from Qwen and cited category-learning studies are not project-specific evidence for the human effect.

claim: Guaranteed safe physical robot execution
criterion: Robot/simulator state-action trajectories and validated enforcement assumptions
finding: No robot or simulator execution is present. Required guarantees are not implemented by the text-generating pipeline. No inference about actual injury, collision rates or deployment safety is possible.

claim: Five orthogonal dimensions and deterministic priority algebra are grounded and sufficient
criterion: Consistent formal definitions, conflict semantics and implementation correspondence
finding: Different documents give different priority relations and force-rate bounds (1.0 versus 1.5 N/s). A product of categories and literary motivation do not establish orthogonality, completeness or safety. Source combines selected contract strings without a formal solver.

claim: Universal linguistic neutrality and phonosemantic benefit
criterion: Cross-language acquisition and label-control experiments
finding: CVCV spelling and short tokenizer length do not establish universal pronounceability, neutrality or cognitive benefit. Current audit label controls test model behavior only.

claim: Original outputs and headline aggregate means exist and can be inspected
criterion: Complete raw condition records with matching arithmetic
finding: All expected active records are present with unique IDs; current EXP002/003 scores reproduce under current evaluator. EXP001 has 11 plan-level reevaluation discrepancies and no frozen historical evaluator. Existence and arithmetic consistency do not independently authenticate historical model execution.

claim: Every table/statistic matches raw data exactly; prior reviews justify 8.2/8.5
criterion: Independent reconstruction of each central numerical and methodological assertion
finding: Current table composite t=4.882 differs from reconstructed 4.62777; abstracts/conclusions mix old and new figures; judge condition is misattributed. Reviewer title and score provide no substitute for these checks. Reviewer provenance/independence is not documented.

claim: Attention drift is an empirically identified cause
criterion: Operational definition plus intervention/measure distinguishing truncation and scoring artifacts
evidence: historical_token_audit.json; historical judge and plan text
finding: 97/100 CoT outputs retokenize near the 300-token cap; all 100 composite outputs reach the 250-token cap. First-five CoT plans often end in deliberation or at the start of the action plan. No attention/activation measurement or causal control is available; truncation is a concrete alternative explanation.

claim: 66.5% catastrophic robot failure
criterion: Distinguish missing textual invariant from completed physical failure event
finding: 66.5% equals one minus archived naive invariant recall (33.5%); current missing-invariant proportion is 65%. Neither is a measured rate of catastrophic robot events or unsafe physical executions.

claim: Project is exactly reproducible with one command
criterion: Pinned environment and model/data revision plus non-destructive execution with complete logs
finding: Local runners, data and outputs are available. Historical model revision/packages are unpinned, absolute Windows paths are embedded, old evaluator state for EXP001 is missing, and orchestrator archives/deletes active outputs. Current audit isolates paths and pins the locally cached snapshot.

claim: CoT increases token generation by 200-300 percent
criterion: Actual complete output token accounting with a defined comparator
finding: For the logged EXP002 outputs, retokenized CoT mean is 299.89 versus naive 199.45, approximately +50.36%, not +200-300%. Historical token IDs/EOS were not saved; retokenization uncertainty is too small to justify the much larger stated factor. Full prompt/call costs are separately measured in new controls.
